messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 170,000 km).  In terms of size, it is the biggest planet we’ve been able to measure directly.  

There are a few other very large exoplanets that have been reported—such as the “super‑Jupiter” HD 106906 b (≈ 1.5 × Jupiter’s radius) and the massive planet around HR 8799—but none exceed HD 100546 b in radius.  If future observations uncover even larger bodies, they will likely be found among the many thousands of exoplanets that have already been detected.
